D2.description: simplicity & cruft: dead code, vestigial names/flags/params, leftover scaffolding, commented-out code — over the production TypeScript sources

D4.description: duplication & drift: copy-paste blocks and renamed copies (token-normalised clone groups), copies that have diverged, and load-bearing parallel implementations that must not drift — over the production TypeScript sources; tests/ duplication is D7's

D6.description: error posture: inconsistent failure honesty between sibling paths — throw-vs-Err, note-vs-silent, fail-open where siblings fail closed, swallowed errors where siblings propagate, load-bearing error-text drift; every finding cites both sides; spec-pinned postures (EXST-9 drop-only, PIC-73 degrade-silent) are pre-exempted — over the production TypeScript sources

D7.description: test quality: silent skips, assertions that cannot fail, boilerplate duplication, copy-paste fixtures/doubles, misleading test names — over the committed test suite; never coverage, never suite composition

D8.description: simplification: complexity disproportionate to the job — over-built mechanisms (speculative generality, pass-through layers, single-use indirection), hand-rolled reimplementations of node/TypeScript/package facilities, API use against the grain, algorithms heavier than their data — accounting and a hypothesised simpler shape, never the fix; the spec is the pin

D9.description: placement & breakdown: code in the wrong module (counted affinity), hollow post-refactor survivors (payload vs scaffolding), and hosts over the size thresholds (files ≥600 / functions ≥60 LOC; presumption of breakdown at ≥1000/≥100, strong at ≥2000/≥200) without a concrete reason to stay whole — accounting and seam hypotheses, never the split design; over the production TypeScript sources

D10.description: verification posture: claim→evidence chains in the fix-record store — fixed/verified claims whose named witness is absent, decayed witness pointers, live-verification claims with nothing citable, evidence presented above its strength; claim wording and pointers only, never test code (D7's), never citation FORM (mechanically gated); over docs/bugs/ and the coverage matrix
